data.summary: Single merged reviewer at fast tier over the 23 source files in development...HEAD. Layering above the repository boundary is correct, core/history is genuinely pure and tested, existing components reused rather than reinvented, and the AC-38 publish->persist->postSideEffect ordering is pinned by a test rather than a comment. Crop clamping, degenerate rects, the crop-name lookup and the rect/bitmap coordinate space were all attacked and hold. One real privacy regression plus eight smaller items.

findings.summary: History archive written with the default umask while the sibling handoff slot in the same ~/.rectify root is deliberately owner-only (0700).
findings.failureScenario: On a shared Linux workstation (~ defaults to 0755) another user reads ~alice/.rectify/history/*/frame.png and strings ~alice/.rectify/rectify.db, obtaining every screenshot, hierarchy dump, annotation comment and prompt Alice ever sent - permanently, since there is no retention policy. The same data inside ~/.rectify/handoff is 0700 and refuses them.

findings.summary: started.elapsedNow() read after the thumbnail encode and history write, inflating the reported send duration.
findings.failureScenario: The first send in a process pays the one-off Skiko native-library load plus a ~1MB frame.png write, the hierarchy XML write and the DB insert before the clock is read; a 0.3s publish is reported to the user as 'Sent 1 note in 0.9 s'.

findings.summary: groupHistory's remember is keyed on state.history only, so the clock is re-read only when the list instance changes.
findings.failureScenario: A tester sends three batches at 23:40 and leaves the panel open overnight (normal for a desktop QA tool); at 09:00 the header over all three still reads TODAY, correcting itself only when the next batch arrives or the app restarts.
findings.note: Fix by also keying on the current local date from a one-per-minute ticker, preserving the single-clock-read purity.

findings.summary: observeAll has no LIMIT and @Relation pulls every child row; the reduced-state justification argues emission frequency, not volume.
findings.failureScenario: At 500 batches x 3 annotations, every send and every app start materialises 500 entities (each carrying the full prompt string the read model discards) + 1500 child rows + 500 thumbnail BLOBs, and ~2-4MB stays parked in MirrorUiState.history for the process lifetime.
findings.note: LIMIT 200 on the observe query, or drop prompt/thumbPng from the list projection and load the thumbnail per row.

findings.summary: First -impl -> -impl module edge in the repo; Room-annotated entities are now on the repository module's compile classpath and in its test fixtures.
findings.failureScenario: The Room backend is no longer swappable behind data-database-api. The leak stops at the repository - nothing Room-shaped reaches domain-usecase-impl or presentation - which is why this is minor.
findings.note: Plan-approved at T-6; recorded, not re-litigated.

findings.summary: Sanitiser regex keeps '.', so a batch id of '..' resolves to File(root, '..'); the comment and the test name both over-claim relative to the code.
findings.failureScenario: write('..', files) writes frame.png into ~/.rectify itself. Unreachable today because mintSessionId always emits <deviceId>-f<n>-<millis>, but the guard will be trusted later by a caller with a different id source.

findings.summary: When the union clamps at the left or top edge, the requested width is preserved rather than the pad.
findings.failureScenario: Union (0,0,100,100) on a 1080-wide frame gives pad 65.7 and left 0, but width stays 231, so the crop extends 131px right of the union instead of 65.7 - the thumbnail of any top-left-corner annotation is visibly off-centre. Appearance only; the rect never leaves the frame.

findings.summary: cropFile(index) is 0-based while the envelope's cropFileName(index) is 1-based; the same image is crop-1.png in the handoff slot and crop-0.png under ~/.rectify/history/<id>/.
findings.failureScenario: Self-consistent within each side, but F-9's diff loop must know both conventions and will mismatch crops if it assumes one.

findings.summary: settleUntil can burn 5s of wall clock waiting out a one-off Skiko load; MirrorUiStateSendFieldTest keeps a now-stale class and file name.
findings.failureScenario: Slow, non-deterministic test time; the next person re-baselining the field test greps for the wrong name.

changeRequests.about: F-1 owner-only permissions on the history archive and ~/.rectify
F-2 hoist the elapsed read above the persist block
F-6 reject blank/./.. batch ids in the path guard

techDebt: F-3 stale Today header when the panel is left open across midnight
F-4 unbounded observe query and unbounded history in reduced state
F-7 thumbnail off-centre when the union clamps at the left/top edge
F-8 crop file index 0-based in history vs 1-based in the handoff envelope
F-9 settleUntil wall-clock cost and the stale SendField test name
CR-5 no Koin DI-graph test for the five new bindings

survey.question: F-1: the history archive is written with the default umask while the ephemeral handoff slot in the same root is deliberately owner-only. How should this land?
options: Fix F-1 on this branch before merge; merge F-2..F-9 as follow-ups
Merge as-is and track F-1 as a follow-up ticket
Request changes: hold until F-1, F-2 and F-3 are all fixed
survey.answer: Fix F-1 on this branch before merge; merge F-2..F-9 as follow-ups
survey.rationale: F-1 turns pruned, owner-only data into a permanent world-readable copy of the tester's screen, and the fix reuses a helper this repo already has for exactly this reason. F-2 and F-6 were also one-liners and were fixed in the same pass.
